summary: A 400-plus-metre elevated path through the forest canopy at Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden in Mae Rim, roughly 20 metres above ground. TAT describes steel-mesh flooring with glass sections and estimates 15–30 minutes to walk; treat it as one stop within the larger garden outing.
whyGo: Get a treetop view across the garden’s mixed forest and surrounding hills from a raised walkway with occasional transparent floor sections.
Pair the short walk with the garden’s glasshouses or trails for a fuller Mae Rim day trip.
bestFor: Visitors who enjoy elevated viewpoints and are comfortable with exposed heights and see-through floor panels.
Nature-focused travellers already planning transport to Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden.
skipIf: You are uncomfortable with heights or open-mesh/glass flooring.
You need a compact attraction close to central Chiang Mai or require confirmed step-free access along the entire route.
duration: Allow 15–30 minutes for the walkway itself, per TAT; add time for queues, photos and the drive between it and other garden attractions. A half-day or longer is a practical estimate for combining it with the wider garden.
cost: The walkway is included in Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden admission, according to TAT. BGO announced revised garden rates effective 1 October 2026: foreign adults ฿250 and foreign children ฿150; verify applicable vehicle or internal transport charges before leaving. Transport and food are extra.
hours: TAT lists the walkway as open daily 08:30–16:30. The wider garden is listed by TAT as open 08:30–17:00; confirm last entry and any temporary closure before travel.
bestTime: Go in the morning for cooler walking, softer light and time to continue around the large garden. December is the cool season, though conditions and visibility vary; the walkway is outdoors and exposed to weather.
gettingThere: The walkway is inside Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden in Mae Rim, outside central Chiang Mai. A private car or prearranged driver is the practical option for the dispersed, hilly site. Arrange a pickup time or return transport before entering; dependable public transport or ride-hailing from the garden was not confirmed.
booking: No separate walkway ticket or advance booking requirement is listed; access is included in garden admission. Check official garden notices or contact the garden before visiting to confirm current hours, fees and walkway operation.
accessibility: TAT describes an elevated route with steel-mesh flooring, glass sections and guard mesh, but does not publish route gradients, lift or ramp details, wheelchair access, or restrictions for visitors with mobility needs. Ask the garden directly about current access and facilities. The exposed height and transparent sections may not suit visitors with vertigo.
practicalTips: Wear secure, comfortable shoes and take care on the mesh surface; avoid relying on the walkway if rain or maintenance affects access.
Bring water, sun protection and a light layer for a cool December morning.
Confirm current garden fees, vehicle charges, hours and walkway status shortly before the visit, especially around the year-end holiday period.
decemberNotes: December is a popular cool-season period in Chiang Mai, and Christmas/New Year can mean more visitors and road traffic. The latest official Botanic Festival dates found were 26 December 2025–4 January 2026; they do not confirm a 2026–27 programme. The revised garden admission rates took effect before this trip period.
uncertainties: The published 15–30-minute duration and daily hours are from TAT; confirm holiday operations and any maintenance closure with the garden.
The BGO tariff notice provides revised garden rates but does not clearly establish vehicle-entry charges; confirm the total on arrival or with the garden.
Current detailed accessibility information and public transport options were not confirmed.
